titulo: First tool: registerTool with inputSchema and execute
lead: A WebMCP tool is an object with a name, a description, an input schema, and an execute function. The page registers it; the agent lists it with getTools and calls it with executeTool. In this lesson you read the kit's search tool, call it the way an agent would, and register your first one.
objetivo: register a tool with a name, description, inputSchema, and execute, and call it the way an agent would, seeing both the result and the screen.

aprende.t: The fields of a tool and the rules for name and description
inputSchema in JSON Schema, closed and described
executeTool: an object goes in, JSON text comes back

hero_alt: A hand fitting a metal connector into a row of empty ports, with a blurred monitor in the background.

nos.detalhe: name (1 to 128 characters: ASCII letters and numbers, _ - .), optional title, non-empty description, inputSchema (JSON Schema), execute(input, { signal }), and optional annotations.
document.modelContext.registerTool(definição, { signal }) returns a Promise with no value. It rejects with InvalidStateError if the name is repeated, breaks the rule, or the description is empty.
Returns the registered tools with name, title, description, inputSchema, annotations, origin, and window. Print only what you need: window does not turn into JSON.
executeTool(ferramenta, objeto, { signal }). The browser runs your execute with the object and returns the result as JSON TEXT (a Promise of a string). Whoever calls it does JSON.parse.
In the kit, the agent's search updates the same list the person sees. The agent and the person see the same state.

secoes.legenda: Spec from 10/16/2026 and Chromium 156.0.8078.4. If it changes, lesson 1 will say so: check the date first.

secoes.sub: Excerpt from kit/pagina/ferramentas.mjs. The same agenda.buscar serves both the form and the tool.

secoes.titulo: Calling it the way an agent would
secoes.sub: listar.mjs runs getTools; executar.mjs runs executeTool with the object you pass and shows the screen afterward.

blocos.conteudo:
cd ~/projetos/formacao-webmcp-site-v72/kit
node scripts/listar.mjs nativo
node scripts/executar.mjs nativo buscar_oficinas '{"tema":"webmcp","apenasComVaga":true}'; echo "saída: $?"

abas.rot: Common mistake: text as input, throw in execute
abas.html:
== Chromium 156.0.8078.4 (Playwright) · modo: nativo
navigator.modelContext (nome antigo): undefined
entrada em texto JSON em vez de objeto: TypeError
execute que lança: UnknownError: Tool was executed but the invocation failed. For example, the script function threw an error
== Chromium 156.0.8078.4 (Playwright) · modo: polyfill
navigator.modelContext (nome antigo): undefined
entrada em texto JSON em vez de objeto: TypeError
execute que lança: UnknownError: Tool execution failed

Old examples passed JSON.stringify(input) to work around a September implementation: today it throws a TypeError in both. And the reason for a throw never reaches the agent (a generic UnknownError). That's why the kit returns { erro } as data (lesson 7).

secoes.sub: The explanation appears after your answer.

perguntas.p: What does executeTool return in the October 16, 2026 spec?
opcoes: A Promise of JSON text with the result.
The object that execute returned, unchanged.
An empty Promise; the result goes to an event.
A RegisteredTool updated with the result.
perguntas.explica: executeTool returns Promise<DOMString>: the browser serializes execute's return value to JSON. The caller does JSON.parse, like testar.mjs.

perguntas.p: Which tool name does registerTool reject?
perguntas.explica: The name accepts 1 to 128 characters: ASCII letters and numbers, _ - and a period. A space isn't allowed, and registration rejects it with InvalidStateError.

perguntas.p: Why does the kit's search call ui.mostrarResultados inside execute?
opcoes: Because the browser requires touching the DOM.
So the person sees the same state the agent received.
So the agent reads the screen instead of the JSON.
Because getTools only lists visual tools.
perguntas.explica: The agent and the person work on the same page. If the agent searches and the screen doesn't change, the person loses the thread. The spec doesn't require it; it's a design decision of the kit.

perguntas.p: A tutorial says to call executeTool(t, JSON.stringify(entrada)). What happens in Chromium 156?
opcoes: It works: the browser accepts text and objects.
It works only in the polyfill, but native Chromium rejects the call.
It works, but the result comes back as an object.
It throws a TypeError: the input must be an object.
perguntas.explica: The input is an object in the spec. The workaround with text came from a September implementation, and today it throws a TypeError in both the native API and the polyfill (measured on 10/19/2026).

itens.texto: A name with a rule, a clear description, a closed inputSchema, and an execute that returns an object.
getTools lists; executeTool takes an object and returns JSON text.
The execute uses the same rule as the form and shows the person what the agent received.
